finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id authorization is never enforced because authorize() is called without await, so the 403 rejection is unobserved and db.reports.remove runs for any session user.
finding.source: Any HTTP DELETE /reports/:id request from a session (req.user set at server.js:5); also when session exists but req.user is undefined.

trace.note: authorize(req.user,'delete',report) called without await; returned Promise rejection is unobserved
Grant lookup db.grants(user.id, resource.id) runs but its outcome does not gate the flow
403 throw becomes a rejected Promise that nothing handles
Delete executes regardless of authorization result

finding.guards_checked: authorize() at server.js:9-16 performs a correct grant check scoped to user.id and resource.id, but the missing await means it never gates the delete. Session middleware at server.js:4-7 only sets req.user; no route-level auth or ownership check exists. Node >=15 unhandled-rejection default may crash the process; not verified at runtime.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 does a real grant check (db.grants(user.id, resource.id), then throws 403 if 'delete' is missing), but its returned promise is never awaited or caught at server.js:20, so the check cannot gate the delete at server.js:21. No route-level auth or ownership check exists in server.js. The only other middleware (server.js:4-7) just copies req.session.user onto req.user.
verdict.reason: At server.js:20 authorize() is called without await, so its rejection is discarded and server.js:21 runs db.reports.remove(report.id) for any session user, including one with no 'delete' grant, because the grant check at server.js:11-14 never gates the delete. Caveat: the candidate's "req.user undefined" source case is loose, since server.js:5 throws for a missing session before the route runs; the core claim holds for any authenticated session user.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id denial path does not return 403: the awaited authorize() throws inside an async Express 4 handler, producing an unhandled rejection, no response, and possible process crash. Availability issue, not a write bypass.
finding.source: PUT /reports/:id from an authenticated user lacking the 'write' grant.
finding.sink: Rejected Promise from authorize() at server.js:14 propagating out of the async route handler
finding.guards_checked: The grant check at server.js:9-16 is correct and awaited, so no bypass exists on this route. Precondition: Express version is not in repo; Express 5 would catch the rejection and return 403.

verdict.guard_found: The grant check authorize() at server.js:9-16 is awaited at line 27, so it correctly denies the write. No try/catch or Express error-handling middleware exists anywhere in server.js to catch the rejected promise. The only other middleware (lines 3-7) does not catch async errors.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match server.js:14, 25-27, but whether the rejection becomes a crash or a 403 depends on the Express version (server.js:1 `require("express")`), and no package.json or lockfile is in the directory: under Express 4 the rejected promise from the async PUT handler at server.js:25-27 is unhandled and can crash the process, while under Express 5 it is caught and returns 403. Separately, the DELETE handler at server.js:20 calls `authorize(...)` without `await`, so a user lacking the 'delete' grant reaches `db.reports.remove` at line 21 — a real write bypass that this candidate does not mention.

finding.claim: Candidate mass assignment: the full client request body is written to the report record, so any column (ownership, tenant, status, visibility, possibly id) a writer sends is persisted. Unverified because the reports schema is not in the repo.
finding.source: req.body parsed by express.json() at server.js:3, with arbitrary client-supplied keys

trace.note: Write grant checked on the same report object (no A/B object mismatch)
Entire req.body passed to update with no field allowlist

finding.guards_checked: Write grant enforced on the correct object via awaited authorize(). No field allowlist, no server-set field handling in server.js. Impact depends on db.reports.update and the reports schema, which are not in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: server.js:27 `await authorize(req.user, "write", report)` is awaited and throws a 403 (server.js:11-14) before the update, so only users holding a write grant on this report reach server.js:28. No field allowlist or server-set field handling exists anywhere in server.js.
verdict.reason: The trace matches server.js:3, 25-28 and the write grant at server.js:27 is effective, so the attacker must be a user already holding write on the report. Whether mass assignment at server.js:28 grants real power (ownership, tenant, or visibility fields) depends on the reports schema and db.reports.update, which are not in the repo, so the impact cannot be decided from the code available.
